construction_notes: Repair limited to the reported build-stage parse error; the frozen population, target, features, splits, thresholds and row checks are unchanged. The failure at line 115 was a typo inside the date-parsing helper: a subscript was written with a space instead of an index expression and the following branch referenced an undefined mask name, so the module could not be imported at all. The helper is now rewritten as a clean format-by-format loop: the raw text is trimmed, blank or sentinel tokens are masked out first, each frozen date format is tried in order with errors coerced, successfully parsed values are written back by index, and any residue gets one lenient inference pass; unparseable nonblank values stay NaT and are still reported by the Closed_Date and Assessed_Penalties parse checks on included rows. No semantic rule was relaxed: unparseable proposed penalties are still excluded and counted, blank assessment or closure still maps to label 0 rather than a zero amount, and nonblank unparseable closure or assessment on an included row still fails. Column resolution, the CPF_Number alias priority, the normalized Case of Probable Violation matching, token splitting and the money-preservation check are carried over unchanged. Source access stays as previously recorded. Unverified and unchanged: there is no full-row historical availability ledger, the 2023 dictionary spells some fields differently from the 2026 raw header, and feature availability at historical notice dates is assumed from current field definitions rather than demonstrated. No holdout row was used for any construction choice.

limitations: Current-vintage extract as of 2026-11-03; historical records may have been revised after case closure, so this is retrospective research rather than a historical forecasting claim.
Right-censoring: cases not closed with a reduction within 36 months are coded zero, so later reductions are missed.
Closed cases with missing Assessed_Penalties are coded zero per the frozen task, not imputed.
Only NOPVs with positive proposed penalties are eligible; warning letters, notices of amendment, corrective action orders and compliance-only cases are excluded.
Cases cluster by operator and sometimes share an inspection; no operator history or lagged outcome features are used, and no corporate-hierarchy reconciliation is attempted.

The data dictionary is dated 2023 and uses some field names that differ from the 2026 raw header; construction follows raw header aliases and fails with observed headers if a required field is absent.
No full-row historical availability ledger exists; feature availability at historical notice dates is assumed from current field definitions and the dictionary.
No causal interpretation: inspection routes, regions and case initiation reflect PHMSA enforcement selection and legal process, not random assignment.
The U.S. public-domain basis is territorial; 17 U.S.C. 105 does not establish a worldwide dedication, and reuse outside the United States may depend on local law.

task.outcome_horizon: 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date; holdout notices end 2023-06-30, so all outcomes are observable by 2026-06-30 against the 2026-11-03 extract.
task.population: NOPV cases with positive Proposed_Penalties and nonmissing Notice_Sent_Date from 2002-01-01 through 2023-06-30; deduplicated to earliest NOPV per WMS_Activity_Seq. Eligibility uses only decision-time information.
task.prediction_time: Notice_Sent_Date, before the operator response, hearing or any order.
task.question: Will a PHMSA Notice of Probable Violation with a proposed civil penalty be closed within 36 months with a lower assessed penalty than proposed?
task.simple_references: Majority class; logistic regression using log(1 + proposed_penalty_usd) alone; calendar-year base rate. No persistence baseline is appropriate because cases are not a regularly sampled time series.
task.split_policy: Fixed chronological boundaries by Notice_Sent_Date: train 2002-01-01 through 2016-12-31; evaluation 2017-01-01 through 2019-12-31; holdout 2020-01-01 through 2023-06-30. No embargo is needed because no lagged outcomes, rolling histories, operator histories or future case records are used; related cases are deduplicated by WMS_Activity_Seq before splitting.
task.target: y is 1 iff the case has a nonmissing Closed_Date no later than 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date and Assessed_Penalties is nonmissing and strictly less than Proposed_Penalties; zero counts as elimination. Otherwise y is 0, including cases not closed with a reduction by 36 months. Closed cases with missing Assessed_Penalties are coded 0, not imputed.
task.title: Will PHMSA proposed pipeline-safety civil penalty be reduced or eliminated within 36 months?
task.usefulness: The proposed demand is known at notice, but the final assessment is not; the task tests whether violation mix, enforcement channel, pipeline segment and proposed amount predict whether PHMSA demand is discounted. It is not a copied status field and supports contest-versus-negotiate triage.

source_access_recipe: Download the publisher raw text file with source_io.fetch from https://primis.phmsa.dot.gov/enforcement-documents/PHMSA%20Pipeline%20Enforcement%20Raw%20Data.txt. The file is not pure UTF-8: decode the downloaded bytes with utf-8-sig first and fall back to cp1252 (then latin-1), recording the encoding that succeeded and asserting zero U+FFFD replacement characters. Parse the decoded text with pandas read_csv from an in-memory buffer using sep=chr(9), quotechar=chr(34), dtype=str, keep_default_na=False and engine='python'. Resolve raw header names case-insensitively with punctuation stripped; the current 53-field header carries CPF_Number (the operator case number, not CPF), WMS_Activity_Seq, Case_Type, Notice_Sent_Date, Proposed_Penalties, Assessed_Penalties, Closed_Date, Violation_Category, Cited_Regulations, Pipeline_Type, Region, How_Discovered? (question mark retained by the publisher), Notice_Actions and Proposed_Compliance_Order_Ind. Keep rows whose Case_Type denotes a Notice of Probable Violation, keep a present and strictly positive Proposed_Penalties, keep a parseable Notice_Sent_Date in 2002-01-01 through 2023-06-30, and deduplicate to the earliest notice per WMS_Activity_Seq. Count list tokens in Violation_Category and distinct tokens in Cited_Regulations. Assign penalty_reduced a value of one when Closed_Date is no later than 36 months after Notice_Sent_Date and Assessed_Penalties is present and strictly below Proposed_Penalties; otherwise use zero. Do not use Assessed_Penalties or Closed_Date as features.
